approachQuestion.prompt: Partition an integer array into the greatest possible number of nonempty contiguous chunks such that sorting each chunk independently and concatenating the sorted chunks produces a globally nondecreasing array. Values may repeat and may be negative. Return the maximum chunk count, not the sorted array. Example: [2,1,3,4,4] returns 4, using [2,1], [3], [4], [4]. Choose the best approach.
constraints: The input is immutable; n is between 1 and 200,000. All integers, indices, counts, and arithmetic results fit in signed 64-bit machine words; comparisons and arithmetic have unit cost.
Input and returned output are excluded from auxiliary space. Working stacks, arrays, and copies count. No hashing is used.

options.text: Scan values with a nondecreasing stack of tentative chunk maxima. If the stack is empty or the current value is at least its top, push it as a new chunk. Otherwise save the top maximum, pop all chunk maxima greater than the current value, and push the saved maximum for the merged chunk. Return stack size.
options.feedback: A smaller new value must merge with each suffix chunk whose maximum exceeds it; otherwise that maximum would precede a smaller value after independent sorting. Earlier chunks with maxima at most the new value remain separable. The merged chunk retains its greatest value.

options.text: Start a new chunk whenever the current value is at least the immediately preceding value; merge only adjacent decreasing pairs.
options.feedback: A later value can invalidate several earlier boundaries. For [2,3,1], all three values must be one chunk, but the initial rise cannot remain a split.

options.text: Use the maxima stack but merge all top maxima greater than or equal to the current value, including equality.
options.feedback: Equal values can be separate sorted chunks. For [2,2], the maximum is 2 chunks, but this merges them into one.

options.text: Try every subset of the n-1 potential boundaries, sort all resulting chunks, and test the concatenation.
options.feedback: It is correct but explores exponentially many partitions and repeatedly sorts, far beyond the declared input size.

feedback.reason: Merge only the suffix of tentative chunks whose maxima invalidate a new boundary.
details: Treat each new value as a potential chunk. If it conflicts with existing suffix maxima, merge that suffix with it and keep the largest maximum from the merged group. Equality does not invalidate a chunk boundary. The number of remaining maxima is the maximum number of chunks.
A new value smaller than an earlier chunk maximum forces those chunks to merge; otherwise independent sorting would cross their boundary. Equality is compatible, so equal maxima do not force a merge.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For merge-conflicting-chunks, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the number of values. Keep only a stack of chunk maxima; do not sort or copy chunks, and return a scalar.
constraints: Stack push, pop, and top take amortized constant time using a growable array; each entry uses a constant number of words. Count the working stack, but exclude input and final output. No recursive call stack or hash table is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each tentative chunk maximum is pushed once and merged away at most once.
details: Each iteration pushes one maximum and each stored entry is popped at most once. The total work is O(n). A nondecreasing input keeps n separate chunk maxima, giving O(n) auxiliary space.
